name: [SSF98] V129
description: A Cepheid in the galaxy M101 that pulsates every 66.1 days.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 66.095 d in Hoffmann et al. (2016), ApJ 830, 10, VizieR J/ApJ/830/10/table5 Gal = M101, ID = 277598 (Per); not a measurement of this star: eq. 2, log R = 0.721 log P + 1.083; the uncertainty is the relation's scatter, 0.067 dex

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, period relations for Galactic fundamental-mode Cepheids applied to this star's period, 66.095 d in Hoffmann et al. (2016), ApJ 830, 10, VizieR J/ApJ/830/10/table5 Gal = M101, ID = 277598 (Per); not a measurement of this star: the luminosity of eq. 1 (M_bol = -2.95 log P - 0.98, with the nominal solar M_bol 4.74) over the radius of eq. 2, through L = 4 pi R^2 sigma T^4 with the nominal solar 5772 K (IAU 2015 Resolutions B2 (Mamajek et al. 2015, arXiv:1510.06262) and B3 (Prsa et al. 2016, arXiv:1605.09788)); the uncertainty is the 317 K by which the two relations miss the paper's own Cepheid temperatures

gravityRange.source: Luck (2018), AJ 156, 171, table 3 (the spectroscopic gravities of its Cepheid spectra)

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity of M101, the Cepheid's galaxy, from 2012A&A...545A..15S; the star's own motion within the galaxy is not measured

distance.source: Placed in M101 as the app draws it, where the star's sight line crosses the disc's midplane: 6,714,829 pc (src/objects/m101-layers/source/recipe.json: centre 6,714,289 pc, inclination 18 deg, line of nodes 219 deg). The galaxy's distance, which places the galaxy and not a star within it: Riess et al. (2016), ApJ 826, 56, Table 5 (Approximations for Distance Parameters), row M101: Cepheid distance modulus mu_Ceph = 29.135 +/- 0.045, d = 6.71 Mpc. (https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.01424); catalogue reference Riess2016ApJ...826...56R: 6714288.52926 pc (-137710.155706/+140593.735267); cepheids

text.card: A Cepheid in the galaxy M101, 6.7 million parsecs away, that swells and shrinks every 66.1 days.
text.introduction: Hoffmann et al. (2016) list its pulsation at 66.1 days.
text.locator: VizieR J/ApJ/830/10/table5 Gal = M101, ID = 277598: Per

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius
Its radius and temperature are what Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33's relations for Galactic Cepheids give at its period; no measurement of this star's size or temperature exists
Its radial velocity is its galaxy's; its own motion within M101 is not measured
